reason: The cited evidence (all from PMC8348113) describes ESD as a technique that produces high-purity coatings with low oxygen concentration under argon, and states that HEA coatings can enhance high-temperature corrosion resistance. However, it provides no experimental data on oxidation resistance of HfNbTaTiZr coatings, no testing in air at 800 °C, and no comparison to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr. The mechanism of a barrier to oxygen diffusion preventing pesting is not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: Electrospark deposition (ESD) can produce HfNbTaTiZr coatings with low oxygen content due to argon shielding
ESD does not induce thermal stress and can improve surface properties
HEA coatings can enhance high-temperature oxidation/corrosion resistance
A homogeneous HfNbTaTiZr alloy can be produced via mechanical alloying and sintering for use as an ESD electrode
